decisions.latin: Si introíero … si ascéndero … Si dédero … et … Et réquiem … donec invéniam
decisions.why: David's vow is the Hebrew oath formula: 'if I enter …' with the curse left unsaid means 'I will not enter'. The Latin keeps the bare *si* (as the Greek εἰ); a Portuguese *Se eu entrar…* is heard as a condition waiting for its main clause, which never comes, and the sense is lost. The glossary row *si of oath* gives the plain negative, applied already at 94:10 (*Não entrarão no meu repouso*) and 88:36 (*não mentirei a Davi*); DRB keeps *If*, MS1932 and every Brazilian text (DM1962, the CNBB) have *Não entrarei … não subirei … não darei*. The two *et* members that continue the third *si* become *nem*.

options.label: Não entrarei … não subirei … não darei … nem … nem
options.note: Draft, the glossary row (94:10, 88:36); MS1932 word for word.

options.label: Se eu entrar … se eu subir … Se eu der … e … e
options.note: The Latin's conditional form (DRB). Refused: heard as an unfinished condition, not as an oath; the vow's sense disappears for a Portuguese ear.

decisions.why: The glossary's pair *lectus → leito*, *stratum → cama* (6:7, 40:4, 62:7) meets here in one phrase, 'the bed of my bedding' (ἐπὶ κλίνης στρωμνῆς μου), which the row said would have to decide locally. The Latin is pleonastic; D2 keeps its two words.

options.label: ao leito da minha cama
options.note: Draft: both nouns kept with the row's words. The phrase is as full as the Latin's; *leito* can also be heard as the lying-place of the bed.

options.label: ao leito em que me deito

forms.strati: ao leito em que me deito

options.note: DRB 'the bed wherein I lie' — turns the noun into a clause and adds a jingle (*leito / deito*).

options.label: ao leito do meu estrado
options.note: MS1932. *estrado* is a platform or a bed-frame in Brazil — refused.

decisions.why: *dormitátio* (νυσταγμός, nodding, dozing) is the noun of *dormitáre*, whose row keeps *dormitar* while *cochilar* is proposed (open). The noun *dormitação* would be unknown. The Latin's order (dative first) keeps *pálpebras*, a proparoxytone, off the final cadence.

options.label: sonolência
options.note: Draft: the plain noun of drowsiness; *dar sonolência* as *dar sono* in the first colon.

options.label: o cochilo
options.note: The dormitáre row's open proposal (*cochilar*; the CNBB LH has *nem cochilarem … minhas pálpebras*); homely.

options.label: adormecimento
options.note: MS1932; heavy, and it is falling asleep rather than dozing.

decisions.why: *témpora* here are the temples of the head (κρόταφοι), the concrete image (rule 5).

options.label: têmporas
options.note: Draft; DRB 'temples'.

options.label: fontes
options.note: MS1932. In Brazil *fontes* is heard as springs first.

decisions.why: *Sicut* (ὡς) after *Meménto … David* says 'how' — what is to be remembered. DRB 'How he swore'; MS1932 supplies *(Lembra-te) que*. The subject is David, from 131:1.

options.label: Como jurou
options.note: Draft: *como* holds 'how' and 'as', the Latin's two senses.

options.label: Como ele jurou
options.note: The hidden subject named (D2 allows); not needed, since *Davi* ends the line before.

decisions.why: The Latin's figura etymologica (ηὔξατο only in the Greek; the Latin makes it noun + verb). The vovére row gives *fazer votos*; *votar* is voting.

options.label: fez um voto
options.note: Draft: the noun kept, the verb is the row's *fazer* (DRB 'vowed a vow').

options.label: votou um voto
options.note: The figure kept, but *votar* is heard as casting a vote — refused.

decisions.why: *audíre* + accusative of a thing is 'hear of' (DRB 'we have heard of it'). *eam* has no antecedent in the Latin (neither *locus* nor *tabernáculum* is feminine); the Church hears the ark of 131:8. The feminine pronoun is kept and nothing named. v2: the place name fronted (stylist) so the mediant is not the proparoxytone *Éfrata*; D28 lets order yield to the ear. *falar* kept although the Latin reader calls it slightly explanatory: the bare *a ouvimos* is heard as a voice.

options.label: ouvimos falar dela
options.note: Draft: *ouvir falar de* is how Portuguese says 'hear of'; the pronoun stays unnamed, as the Latin's. MS1932 *ouvimos dizer que a arca estava* names the ark (a gloss, refused).

options.label: a ouvimos
options.note: Literal; heard as hearing a sound or a woman's voice in Ephrata.

decisions.why: The stare row's *estar de pé* cannot take feet as subject; 121:2 *Stantes erant pedes nostri* went to *deter-se* (*Os nossos pés se detinham*), and this is the same build. v2: the Latin reader: *stare* is standing, *se deter* adds arrested motion; 121:2 had *erant stantes* after a journey, 131:7 has none. *estiveram* taken.

options.label: estiveram os seus pés
options.note: v2 ruling: plain, the verb the Latin has (the Latin reader).

options.label: se detiveram os seus pés
options.note: v1 draft, after 121:2; refused in v2 as adding motion.

options.label: pousaram os seus pés
options.note: MS1932; *pousar* is alighting, not standing.

decisions.why: *in* + accusative gives the rising a direction: 'arise into your rest'. The glossary gives *Surge / Exsúrge → Levantai-vos* (81:8). Brazil sings the Hebrew-based *Subi, Senhor, para o lugar de vosso pouso* (the Assumption vigil refrain, fetched — `ps131/circulation.md`); *subir* is not the Latin's verb.

options.label: para o vosso repouso
options.note: Draft: *para* carries the Latin's direction; the Brazilian refrain has the same preposition.

options.label: ao vosso repouso
options.note: As 114:7 *Volta … ao teu repouso*; after *levantar-se* it is weaker.

options.label: e entrai no vosso repouso
options.note: MS1932 and Portugal's lectionary supply a verb — refused, a word the Latin lacks.

decisions.latin: arca sanctificatiónis tuæ … efflorébit sanctificátio mea
decisions.why: Both are ἁγίασμα in the Greek (checked in the parallels), the Greek of 77:54 and 95:6, where the open sanctificátio row keeps *santificação*. The Latin repeats its word at the two ends of the psalm's second half; the Portuguese keeps one word for both. (96:12 went to *santidade* because its Greek is ἁγιωσύνη.)

options.label: santificação
options.note: Draft, the row. The ambiguity reader of 95:6 did not know the word — the cost.

options.label: santidade
options.note: MS1932 in both places; plainer, but it is *sánctitas*'s word.

options.label: que santificastes (131:8)
options.note: DRB 'which thou hast sanctified' — a clause for the genitive; only in 131:8.

decisions.why: The object *veritátem* stands without article. Verb first as the Latin (and as 109:4 *Jurou o Senhor*). *David* indeclinable, the Greek's dative τῷ Δαυιδ. v2: the stylist heard three unstressed *a*s run together (*a verdade a Davi … não a*). The subject is put first and the object pronoun made enclitic in *há de frustrá-la*.

options.label: O Senhor jurou a Davi a verdade

forms.veritatem: O Senhor jurou a Davi a verdade

options.note: v2 ruling (stylist): the plain order; *a verdade* at the caesura then carries *frustrá-la*.

options.label: Jurou o Senhor a verdade a Davi

forms.veritatem: Jurou o Senhor a verdade a Davi

options.note: Draft: *jurar a verdade* is sayable; the following *a* (it) then points to the truth, as *eam*.

options.label: Jurou o Senhor a Davi a verdade

forms.veritatem: Jurou o Senhor a Davi a verdade

options.note: The Latin's order; *a Davi a verdade* stacks three *a*s.

options.label: Jurou o Senhor uma verdade a Davi

forms.veritatem: Jurou o Senhor uma verdade a Davi

decisions.why: *frustrári* (deponent): to deceive, to make vain (L&S); the Greek ἀθετήσει 'will not set it aside'. Portuguese *frustrar* is 'to make fail, bring to nothing' — the cognate carries the sense. v2: *não a frustrará* dropped with the order change; *não há de frustrá-la* keeps the cognate, puts the pronoun after the verb (no *não a* cluster), and gives a paroxytone at the mediant. The ambiguity reader did not know *frustrar* for an oath, which is the cost of the cognate.

options.label: não há de frustrá-la
options.note: v2 ruling (stylist).

options.label: não a frustrará
options.note: Draft, the cognate.

options.label: não a anulará
options.note: The Greek's sense; another word.

options.label: não deixará de cumpri-la
options.note: MS1932 — explains; refused.

decisions.latin: Et fílii eórum usque in sǽculum
decisions.why: *Et* opens the main clause after the condition of 12a: 'their sons also'. A Portuguese *E* at the head of an apodosis is heard as a second condition.

options.label: Também os filhos
options.note: Draft; MS1932 and DM1962 *também*.

options.label: E os filhos
options.note: Literal.

decisions.why: The habitátio row gives *habitação*; *para sua habitação* ends the verse in *-ão* against *Sião* at the mediant, a rhyme the Latin does not have (rule 5). The Latin's order puts the possessive after.

options.label: para habitação sua
options.note: Draft: the Latin's order, no rhyme; slightly formal.

options.label: para sua habitação
options.note: MS1932; the natural order, rhymes with *Sião*.

decisions.why: *eam* may be Sion (13) or *réquies* (both feminine in Latin; the Greek αὐτήν and κατάπαυσις too). Portuguese must choose a gender: *a* points to Sião, *o* to *repouso*. The feminine repeats 13b *escolheu-a* (*elégit eam*) word for word, which the Latin does.

options.label: a escolhi
options.note: Draft: Sion, the echo of 13b.

options.label: o escolhi
options.note: MS1932: the rest.

decisions.why: Participle + finite verb of one root, the Hebraic intensive (εὐλογῶν εὐλογήσω); D2 keeps the repetition. Verb: the open benedícere (God → man) row keeps *bendizer* (133:3, 127:5); every Brazilian text says *abençoar*. *viúva*: the Latin (with a Greek variant χήραν) where the Rahlfs text and the Hebrew have 'her provision' — the Latin is followed.

options.label: Bendizendo, bendirei a sua viúva
options.note: Draft: the figure and the row's verb, in Portuguese order.

options.label: Abençoando, abençoarei a sua viúva
options.note: The familiar verb, if the row moves to *abençoar*.

options.label: A sua viúva, bendizendo, bendirei
options.note: The Latin's order, object first — an inversion for its own sake in Portuguese.

options.label: Abençoarei copiosamente a sua viúva
options.note: MS1932 — dissolves the repetition; refused.

decisions.why: Plural *panes* for bread is the Latin's idiom (ἄρτων); D42 settled *o meu pão* for *panes* at 41:4. *saturáre → saciar* (row).

options.label: de pão
options.note: Draft (D42); DM1962 *fartarei de pão*.

options.label: de pães
options.note: MS1932; the Latin's number.

decisions.why: Noun + verb of one root (ἀγαλλιάσει ἀγαλλιάσονται), which answers 131:9 *et sancti tui exsúltent*. D2 keeps the repetition; the exsultáre row gives *exultar / exultação*; 125:6b *cum exsultatióne → com exultação*.

options.label: exultarão com exultação
options.note: Draft: the figure kept, with the instrumental *com*.

options.label: exultarão de exultação
options.note: *de* for the ablative of cause; heavier.

options.label: exultarão de alegria
options.note: The CNBB's (from the Hebrew); loses the repetition — refused.

decisions.why: *prodúcere* here renders ἐξανατελῶ, 'make to spring up' (as a plant); L&S gives 'bring forth, produce' of growing things. 103:14 *prodúcens fænum* → *produzindo*, where the object is the grass itself.

options.label: farei brotar
options.note: Draft: the causative of springing (DM1962 *Farei brotar*, from the Hebrew, where the image is the same).

options.label: produzirei
options.note: The cognate; 'produce a horn' sounds made.

options.label: farei surgir
options.note: Plainer, loses the growing.

decisions.why: *David* is indeclinable: genitive ('David's horn') or dative ('a horn for David'). The Greek is dative (κέρας τῷ Δαυιδ) and the second colon's *Christo meo* is dative, so the verse is a pair of gifts. *cornu → chifre* (row). v2: the genitive adopted — the Latin reader for the word, and the stylist and ambiguity readers both heard *pôr chifre* (cuckoldry) in *um chifre para Davi*, which the genitive removes; the two colons stay parallel as two things God makes ready.

options.label: o chifre de Davi
options.note: v2 ruling: genitive, the Latin read as it stands (DRB margin, MS1932 *o poder de David* with its gloss removed). Keeps the horn-image and loses the colloquial echo.

options.label: um chifre para Davi
options.note: v1 draft: dative with the Greek and DRB. Refused in v2: *chifre para alguém* is heard as cuckoldry in Brazil (stylist, ambiguity).

options.label: a Davi um chifre
options.note: Keeps the Latin's double reading as far as Portuguese can; the order is forced.

choices.131:1: The second colon is the Vespers antiphon *Et omnis * mansuetúdinis ejus* and reads alone: *E de toda a sua mansidão*. *mansuetúdo → mansidão* as 44:5b, 89:10b (the Latin with the Greek πραΰτης, against the Hebrew 'hardships'). No titulus (D7).
choices.131:3: tabernáculum → *tenda* (row), here a man's tent, as God's in 131:5 and 131:7 — the psalm plays one against the other. Length flag 3a (−4) accepted: the oath's plain future is shorter than the Latin's conditional (si_oath).
choices.131:5: *donec invéniam* → *até que encontre* (v2: the supplied *eu* dropped at the stylist's word; *minhas têmporas* keeps the first person). *réquies → repouso* (row), the same noun as 131:8 and 131:14. *Deus Jacob → o Deus de Jacó* (formula). Length flag 5a (+3 in v2) accepted: *até que encontre um lugar para o Senhor* has no shorter sayable form.
choices.131:6: *nós a encontramos*: the pronoun is proclitic after a named subject (not the bookish *encontramo-la*). *silva → selva* (D44), *campi → campos*. *selva* kept against the stylist's *bosque*: D44 ruled it (*silva* is one word through the psalter).
choices.131:7: The first colon is the Dedication versicle *Introíbimus in tabernáculum ejus* and reads alone. Future kept (*Entraremos*, *adoraremos*); the CNBB's hortatives *Entremos … prostremo-nos* are the Hebrew's. Length flag 7a (−4) accepted: *tenda* (row) against *tabernáculum*.
choices.131:8: The versicle of Pasc4-0 (TemporaM) and C4c. *Levantai-vos* is the glossary's form for *Surge / Exsúrge* (81:8, 3:7). Length flag 8a (+3) accepted: *para o vosso* is the Latin's possessive.
choices.131:9: The Preces versicle *V. Sacerdótes tui induántur justítiam. R. Et sancti tui exsúltent* — each colon reads alone. *induántur* + accusative → *se vistam de* as 34:26b *Vistam-se de vergonha*; subject first as the Latin, proclisis after the subject. *sancti (ὅσιοι) → santos* (row).
choices.131:10: *Propter → por causa de* (row); *avértere fáciem → desviar a face* (row); *Christus → Cristo* (D19 names this verse). *Davi, vosso servo* without article, as 77:70 *Davi, seu servo* and 88:21.
choices.131:11: God speaks to David: *tu* (D17). The second colon is the Christmas antiphon *De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam* and reads alone: *Do fruto do teu ventre * porei sobre o teu trono* (partitive *de*, as MS1932). *fructus ventris → o fruto do ventre* as 126:2b; *sedes → trono* (row).
choices.131:12a: A real condition here (not the oath of 131:3). *testaméntum → aliança* (row), *testimónia → testemunhos* (D15), *docére → ensinar* (row). *hæc* kept as *estes*.
choices.131:12b: *usque in sǽculum → para todo o sempre* (D37). *sedébunt super sedem tuam* repeats 11's *super sedem tuam* → *sobre o teu trono* both times.
choices.131:13: *elégit … elégit* kept twice (the Greek varies its verb; the Latin does not). *habitátio → habitação* (row).
choices.131:14: *in sǽculum sǽculi → pelos séculos dos séculos* (D27); the formula puts a proparoxytone at the mediant, as at 44:7. *habitáre → habitar*. Length flag 14a (+4) accepted: the D27 formula.
choices.131:16: God's answer to 131:9: *justítiam → salutári*, *exsúltent → exsultatióne exsultábunt*. *salutáre → salvação* (D6). With 131:17 the Gradual of C4-1 and 10-23r.
choices.131:17: *Illuc → Ali*. *parávi* perfect kept (*preparei*), against the future of the first colon, as the Latin. *lucérna → lâmpada* as 17:29, 118:105. *Christo meo → para o meu Cristo* (D19). v2: with the genitive (decision cornu) the flags on 17a (+3) and 17b (+4) are accepted for *para o meu Cristo*.
choices.131:18: *confúsio → vergonha* and *índuere … confusióne → vestir de vergonha*, as 34:26b and 108:29. *efflorescere → florescer* as 102:14. *super ipsum → sobre ele*.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps131.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932, DM1962); DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Liturgical uses by grep of DO Latin and Brazilian circulation fetched, not asserted — both in ps131/circulation.md (CNBB LH page saved as consult/web-lh-salmo-131-132.html; CNBB Bible consult/bolls-CNBB-19-132.json; the Brazilian Assumption-vigil refrain *Subi, Senhor, para o lugar de vosso pouso* from search results only). Glossary and finished psalms consulted with ps131/gloss_look.py and ps131/concord.py. Hard readings: the oath *si* (3–5), *lectum strati mei*, *audívimus eam*, *sanctificátio* (8, 18), *benedícens benedícam* and *exsultatióne exsultábunt*, *cornu David* (genitive or dative), *elégi eam*.

render.py + checks.py: hard checks pass (ids, pointing). Soft flags are length only (131:3a, 5a, 7a, 8a, 14a, 17a, 17b), all accepted in choices['131:length']. The one accidental rhyme found, *Sião / habitação* in 131:13, was removed in the draft by the ruling on sibi.
No critical or major issue; six minors.
